questions.stem: Replacing the side chain of alanine with hydrogen produces which amino acid?

choices.explanation: Alanine retains a methyl side chain; the replacement changes its identity.
Glycine has hydrogen as its side chain, giving two hydrogens on the alpha carbon.
Valine has a branched carbon side chain rather than hydrogen.
Serine has a hydroxymethyl side chain rather than hydrogen.

questions.stem: An alpha carbon is attached to amino, carboxyl, hydrogen, and methyl groups. Which feature makes it a chiral center?

choices.text: It has a double bond to oxygen.
choices.explanation: The carbon described has four single bonds; the carboxyl group contains the oxygen double bond.
Identical groups prevent this tetrahedral carbon from being a chiral center.
Four distinct groups on this tetrahedral carbon permit two mirror-related configurations.
A methyl group contains carbon and hydrogen; nitrogen in the side chain is not required for chirality.
